mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are likely to improve.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 20-day horizon more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 4% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If unemployment rises above 4% but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When employment increases but unemployment does not decrease, it may indicate labor market inefficiencies, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If employment rises without a corresponding drop in unemployment, but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in federal funds rate leads to higher borrowing costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If federal funds rate increases but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time during the tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation as indicated by CPI leads to negative real returns, impacting S&P 500 negatively.
failure_condition: If CPI is high but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts indicates weaker demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If housing starts fall below 1200 but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production without corresponding GDP growth may indicate supply-side issues, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases without GDP growth but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rapid growth in real disposable income may lead to overconsumption and economic imbalance, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns in the late expansion phase.
failure_condition: If real disposable income grows rapidly but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time during late-cycle.
